Mali.title: Mali: Army conducts targeted strikes against armed groups in several regions
Mali.summary: Mali: the army carries out targeted strikes against armed groups in several regions These interventions are part of Operation Dougoukoloko, dedicated to the surveillance, control and security of the national territory, specifies the military command.

Mali.title: Violent armed confrontations.. Moroccan drivers face death on the roads of Mali
Mali.summary: Moroccan trucks survived a shooting in Mali yesterday, Thursday, after they tried to pass through their goods in this African country that lives under the weight of war, and this incident prompted professionals to launch a wide appeal to avoid this corridor.

Mali.title: New robberies reported on Gao-Intilit axis
Mali.summary: The robberies of transport buses are multiplying on the Gao-Intilit axis, arousing the concern of travellers. After a first attack last Tuesday, another bus was reportedly held up this Thursday on the same route. The passengers were reportedly stripped of their belongings, while their luggage and parcels were searched and ransacked.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: Fama strikes several terrorist targets in the Doïla and Djénné areas
Mali.summary: Bamako, October 30 (AMAP) The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, the General Staff of the Armed Forces said in a statement on Friday. According to the same source, the exploitation of precise information on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, made it possible to locate, north of the village of Talhandak, a strategic regroupment point housing armed terrorist groups as well as war material and logistics.

Mali.title: From Mali to Niger, is secret disappearance becoming a method of government in the ESA?
Mali.summary: In Mali, opponent Mountaga Tall and her son remain unaccounted for six months after their abduction. In Niger, the government admits to detaining journalist Moussa Kaka, but still refuses to indicate where and why. In both cases, relatives and lawyers do not know where the three men are locked up.

Mali.title: An opponent of the junta in Mali, victim of an enforced disappearance
Mali.summary: - HRW, October 30, 2026 Mountaga Tall and his son must be located and released More »Mountaga Tall and his son must be located and released. Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, who had openly criticized the junta in Mali, and her son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, are still missing; their whereabouts are unknown and the Malian authorities remain silent .

Mali.title: Mali: Targeted army strikes against terrorist logistics
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, carried out on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 a series of targeted strikes against several terrorist groups in the North, Southeast and Center of the country, announced the General Staff of the Armed Forces in a statement released Friday in Bamako These combined interventions are part of the Dougoukoloko operation, dedicated to the surveillance, control and security of the national territory, reported Friday the general staff of the Malian army.

Mali.title: Terrorism tracked and neutralized: FAMa successfully strikes in Talhandak, Nangola and Djenné
Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, north of the village of Talhandak, a strategic regroupment point housing armed terrorist groups as well as war and logistics equipment.

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: the FAMa strike terrorist positions in several localities
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, continue their operations to monitor and secure the territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. The General Staff of the Armed Forces gave an update on several strikes carried out on Wednesday, October 28, 2026 . North of the village of Talhandak, precise information made it possible to locate a major terrorist assembly point, where war materiel and logistics were stored.

Mali.title: Mali: L'armée et l'Africa corps russe déciment plus de 200 têtes de bétail près de Diéma
Mali.summary: Au Mali, plus de 200 boeufs et moutons ont été tués mercredi 28 octobre par l'armée malienne et ses partenaires russes de l'Africa Corps à Mangara, commune de Dioumara, cercle de Diéma, dans la région de Nioro du Sahel. Des habitations ont également été incendiées. C'est le deuxième incident similaire en huit jours.

Mali.title: Mali: An opponent of the Malian junta has been the victim of an enforced disappearance for six months
Mali.summary: Mountaga Tall and her son must be located and released Six months after their abductions, Mountaga Tall, who had openly criticized the junta in Mali, and her son, Cheick Mamadou Tall, are still missing; their whereabouts are unknown and the Malian authorities remain silent. Every day that goes by without news causes fear for their safety and aggravates the anguish of their family Unidentified gunmen abducted Mountaga Tall in Mali's capital Bamako on May 2.

Mali.title: DCSSA/DMHTA: the Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces on an authority visit to both structures
Mali.summary: As part of his command tour with the staffs and service directorates of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), the Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (CEMGA), Major General Elisée Jean DAO, visited, on Thursday, October 29, 2026, the garrison of Kati, where he visited successively the Central Directorate of the Army Health Service (DCSSA) and the Directorate of Equipment, Hydrocarbons and Transport of At the DCSSA, the CEMGA was welcomed by the director of the structure, Brigadier General Guediouma DEMBÉLÉ.

Mali.title: Mali: Russian army and Africa Corps decimate more than 200 head of cattle near Diéma
Mali.summary: Mali: the army and the Russian Africa Corps decimate more than 200 head of cattle near Diéma In Mali, more than 200 cattle and sheep were killed on Wednesday 28 October by the Malian army and its Russian partners of the Africa Corps in Mangara, Dioumara commune, Diéma circle, in the Nioro region of the Sahel. Homes were also set on fire. This is the second similar incident in eight days .

Mali.title: Dem/DSMIL: The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces on an authority visit to both structures
Mali.summary: The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (CEMGA), Major General Elisée Jean DAO, made visits to the Directorate of Military Schools (dem) and the Directorate of Military Sports (DSMIL) on Tuesday, 27 October 2026. . These visits are part of his series of visits to the headquarters and service directorates of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), aimed at inquiring about their functioning and recalling the directions of the command.

Mali.title: Mali: Dead and wounded in clashes between "Dozo" and al-Qaeda militants near Jeni
Mali.summary: Al-Mayadeen

Niger.title: Niger, Human Rights Watch and RSF demand Moussa Kaka's release
Niger.summary: Les deux organisations de défense des journalistes ont à nouveau réclamé la libération du correspondant de RFI au Niger, ainsi que la transparence sur sa situation. Par la rédaction de Mondafrique L’arrestation du journaliste, le 31 août, deux jours après le coup d’État manqué du 29, a d’abord été secrète. Il s’est volatilisé avec son véhicule sur la route de son domicile, après sa journée de travail dans sa radio et télévision privée Saraounia.

Mali.title: DIRECTORATE OF MILITARY JUSTICE: seven cases scheduled for the correctional hearing
Mali.summary: The Military Court of Bamako held, on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, a correctional hearing at its premises, located in Dar Salam. The session was chaired by Magistrate Assama DOLO, assisted by his fellow magistrates. In total, seven cases were on the list for this hearing.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Macina: The closing of Solidarity and Social Exclusion Month at the centre of a meeting
Mali.summary: Macina, October 29 (AMAP) The Prefect of Circle, Albaraka Ag Amarizag, chaired this Wednesday, in the conference room of his constituency in Macina, a meeting on the closing of the month of Solidarity and social exclusion, noted AMAP . It was in the presence of the deputy mayor, Mamadou Almamy Tangara, the sub-prefect of Kolongotomo, the FAMa coordinator, and the acting head of the local development and solidarity economy department, Mr.

Mali.title: Mali: General Amadou Haya Sanogo appointed as head of the Board of Directors of the National Office of Veterans Affairs
Mali.summary: A new institutional responsibility was entrusted to Lieutenant General Amadou Haya Sanogo. By Decree No. 2026-0648/PT-RM of 22 October 2026, the President of the Transition, Head of State, Army General Assimi Goïta, appointed him Chairman of the Board of Directors of the National Office of Former Combatants, Retired Military Members and War Victims of Mali (ONAC-M) .

Mali.title: Mali War School: the 6th class is back in school
Mali.summary: The Mali War School (EGM) launched, on Thursday, October 22, 2026, the academic activities of its 6th class in Badalabougou, Bamako. The ceremony was presided over by the Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces, Major General Elisée Jean Dao, in the presence of the director of the establishment, Major General Oumar Dao, and several partners . The inaugural lesson was moderated by Mamadou Tièny Konaté, Second Vice-President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Mali (CCIM).

Mali.title: Mali: Dozo hunters and jihadists clash for a village near Djenné
Mali.summary: In Mali, the village of Sounga, which belongs to the commune of Mougna, near Djenné in the Mopti region, continues to resist the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda. While the surrounding villages have bowed to the domination of the jihadists, Sounga refuses to submit, provoking violent clashes last week between the Jnim jihadists and the traditional Dozo hunters, who strive to protect the population in this part of the territory where the Malian army is not present.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Russia-Africa: Moscow says it is ready to help the continent against terrorism
Mali.summary: Bamako, Oct. 29 (AMAP) Russia is ready to help its African partners fight terrorism, drug trafficking and cross-border crime, Russian President Vladimir Putin said during a meeting with representatives of major African regional organizations, organized as part of exchanges between Moscow and institutions on the continent, according to the TASS news agency The Russian head of state reaffirmed his country's willingness to continue close coordination with the African Union on a wide range of foreign policy issues.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Macina: meeting of the local watch committee coupled with that of crises and disasters
Mali.summary: Macina, 29 October (AMAP) A meeting of the watch committee, coupled with that of crises and disasters, took place yesterday Wednesday, in Macina under the chairmanship of the Prefect of Circle, Albaraka Ag Amarizag, noted AMAP . It was in the presence of Deputy Mayor Mamadou Almamy Tangara, the FAMa coordinator, the acting head of the local development and solidarity economy department, Mr.

Mali.title: Bamako: twelve suspects arrested in three criminal cases
Mali.summary: Three police stations in Bamako, those of ACI 2000, Sébénikoro and Boulkassoumbougou, arrested twelve suspects in three separate criminal cases that occurred in October 2026. The first case dates back to October 14. The body of a 23-year-old man was discovered in a gutter .

Mali.title: Mali: Dozo hunters and jihadists clash for a village near Djenné
Mali.summary: In Mali, the village of Sounga, which belongs to the commune of Mougna, near Djenné in the Mopti region, continues to resist the jihadists of Jnim, linked to al-Qaeda While the surrounding villages have bowed to the domination of the jihadists, Sounga refuses to submit, provoking violent clashes last week between the Jnim jihadists and the traditional Dozo hunters, who are trying to protect the populations in this part of the territory where the Malian army is not present .

Mali.title: Mali: Turkish drones and Russian command, the responsibilities behind the deadly strikes
Mali.summary: In Mali, air strikes presented by the army as operations against armed groups have killed civilians, including children. On September 16, 2026, an investigation by Bellingcat and Jeune Afrique reconstructed several bombings from satellite images, videos and testimonies . A report published the same day by the NGO The Sentry examines the conditions of purchase of Turkish drones and the role of Russian commanders in operations.

Mali.title: Menaka: 54 bodies discovered in a...
Mali.summary: Menaka: 54 bodies discovered in a camp in Tagadeyat The General Staff of the Armed Forces announced, in a statement, the macabre discovery of 54 lifeless bodies about 35 kilometers south-east of Menaka. Nine survivors were also found and evacuated to the city. The first testimonies attribute these killings to the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara (EIGS).

Mali.title: Press/West Africa: strike in Senegal, price drop in Mali and major economic projects
Mali.summary: The continuation of the general strike in Senegal, the announced fall in meat prices in Mali and investment projects in Ghana are among the topics that are attracting the attention of the West African press on Thursday. In Burkina Faso, the dialogue with Türkiye focuses in particular on security and investments, while Benin opens its budget session on several legislative and social priorities In Senegal, the Front syndical pour la défense du travail (FSDT) claims a success rate of 90% for the first day of its general strike organized Wednesday, October 21, Pressafrik reports.

Mali.title: Bamako Grand Market: Two suspects...
Mali.summary: Great Market of Bamako: Two suspects arrested, 290 million CFA francs in damage and a trailer truck seized! By patiently following up the trail of several burglaries committed between 2023 and 2026, Chief Commissioner Josué KAMATÉ and his investigators from the Police Station of the Shopping Centre managed to identify two suspects. Eighteen shops were reportedly targeted, including fourteen at the Bamako Grand Market .

Burkina Faso.title: Military cooperation: opening of the second session of the Joint Monitoring Committee Burkina Faso-Egypt
Burkina Faso.summary: (Ouagadougou, October 27, 2026) – The Ministry of War and Patriotic Defence (MGDP) hosted, on October 27, 2026 in Ouagadougou, the opening ceremony of the second session of the Joint Monitoring Committee for Military and Technical Cooperation between the Arab Republic of Egypt and Burkina Faso Scheduled for two days, the work was opened by the Comrade Secretary General of the MGDP, Intendant Colonel-Major Yamba Léonard OUOBA.

Niger.title: Niger: Journalist Moussa Kaka 'Enforced Disappearance', Denounces Human Rights Watch
Niger.summary: Journalist Moussa Kaka, reported missing and then declared detained in Niger, is the victim of an "enforced disappearance", denounced Thursday the NGO Human Rights Watch (HRW) which demands that the authorities reveal his place of detention. Niger has been ruled since 2023 by a military regime resulting from a coup d 'état, regularly accused by NGOs of repression, including attacks on press freedom.

Niger.title: Algeria Starts Arrangements to Send Troops to Niger to Protect Energy Projects
Niger.summary: Algeria begins arrangements to send troops to Niger to protect energy projects - Algerian forces will be stationed in the vicinity of the Kafra field north of Niger, where Cepax, Sonatrach and Sonadip are engaged in oil exploration, taking advantage of geographical proximity to provide air coverage and an effective supply line.

Niger.title: Algeria prepares troop deployment in Niger to protect oil assets and expand influence
Niger.summary: The day after Algeria’s parliament authorised a military intervention in Niger on 25 October, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced plans to “protect Algeria’s energy interests” and implement a military and security cooperation agreement signed with Niamey on 21 October. Niger.title: Chad and Niger squabble over drone strike
Niger.summary: The diplomatic crisis that has just erupted between Niger and Chad since a Chadian drone strike in Niger on October 24, has highlighted the growing tensions between the two countries for several months, where Paris plays an amplifying role . But it is unlikely to grow beyond the exchange of bird names, given the importance of good neighbourly relations between the two countries, which share a wide border, populations, enemies and sustained exchanges .

Niger.title: Drone in Niger: Algeria, the future aerial shield of Niamey?
Niger.summary: The disputed attack in northern Niger gives a new scope to the expected Algerian military deployment in Madama. Beyond oil interests, Algiers could provide its neighbor with the surveillance capabilities essential for the control of this huge border area . The international investigation requested by Niamey, and to which N’Djamena is in favour, will have to establish who hit the Emiloulou area, in the Niger region of Agadez, on 24 October.

On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others. The first would have won, claiming to have neutralized 400 men of the GSIM and seized 100 of their motorcycles as well as hundreds of weapons.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso’s unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code that restores the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and importation of expired or prohibited products. The country had abolished the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 2018 while its last known judicial execution took place in 1988. Reinstating capital punishment sends a chilling message to critics of the military junta and risks becoming another tool to suppress dissent.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso's junta reinstates the death penalty The military regime had officially announced its intention to reinstate the death penalty by passing a bill last December. It had been abolished in 2018.
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso reintroduced the death penalty into a new penal code on Tuesday, October 20, after a unanimous vote of the unelected members of the People's Legislative Assembly (PLA), which serves as the parliament in the junta-run country. At the head of the military regime that came to power at the end of September 2022 by a coup d 'état, Captain Ibrahim Traoré governs the country with an iron fist Dozens of critical voices, as well as journalists and magistrates have been kidnapped and sometimes forcibly conscripted to fight the jihadists who are undermining the country, according to international NGOs.

Niger.title: Chad-Niger: N’Djamena rejects accusations of drone strikes in Agadez

Niger.title: Drone strike in Agadez: Chad's ambassador summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
Niger.summary: The Minister of Justice, Keeper of the Seals, Mr. Alio Daouda, acting Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad, H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangaré, received on Tuesday, October 27, 2026 the Ambassador of the Republic of Chad in Niger, as part of the summons relating to the drone strike in the Agadez region This measure follows a drone airstrike that occurred on October 24, 2026, around 1 a.m., in the Emiloulou area, Agadez region.

Niger.title: Image Africa Niger: Chad denies any involvement in a "drone strike" on its soil with the "support" of France
Niger.summary: On Tuesday, October 27, Chad rejected accusations from Niger, a neighboring country with which relations have been tense for several months. The latter accuses him of having killed two civilians in a "drone strike" on Nigerien soil with the "support" of France. Through its spokesperson, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, N’Djamena categorically denied Niamey's accusations about a drone strike on Nigerian soil on Monday, October 26 .

Niger.title: Analysis. Chad-Niger tensions: how the Sahel is becoming a proxy conflict terrain Sahel Horizon
Niger.summary: The accusation made by the Nigerien authorities against Chad, after a deadly drone strike on 24 October 2026 in Nigerien territory [in the Emi Lulu area, in the Agadez region, near the Algerian border], marks a new stage in the crisis between the two countries. Niamey reports two civilians killed and several injured . The government announces that it wants to refer the matter to the UN Security Council and the African Union.

Niger.title: Niger accuses Chad of drone attack that killed two civilians
Niger.summary: As their relations continue to deteriorate, Niger’s military government on Monday accused Chad of carrying out a deadly drone strike in which two civilians were killed and others wounded. In a statement by the authorities read on national television, it said it had summoned the Chadian ambassador following the incident. Niamey also demanded an immediate end to "hostile actions" and compensation for the damage caused.

Niger.title: Portrait Article reserved for our subscribers Chérif Ould Taher, the sulphurous Malian intermediary behind the last hostage releases in the Sahel Kidnapped in 2025 by the Islamic State in the Sahel, a Swiss woman and an Austrian woman were released on Wednesday. As for an American, in August, this businessman, considered one of the main drug traffickers in northern Mali, played a key role.
Niger.summary: They had been abducted three months apart in Agadez, in northern Niger, where they had lived for many years. The Austrian Eva Gretzmacher, 74, and the Swiss Claudia Abbt, 68, respectively kidnapped in January and April 2025 by the Islamic State in the Sahel (ISIS), were released Wednesday, October 21 . Presumably held in the sanctuary of the jihadist group, in the Menaka region of neighboring Mali, they were recovered in southern Libya by a unit of the Libyan National Army of Marshal Khalifa Haftar and taken by plane to Benghazi, the stronghold of the strongman of eastern Libya .

Good day. This is Sultana Al-Qahtani with the Sahel Desk.

Daily bottom line for 2026-10-28: Reporting dated 2026-10-28 gives the desk 3 incident accounts to examine in Mali. 2 have support from separate sources. The record is provisional; it does not establish the full extent of violence that day.

Mali: 28 retained reports. 1. Crime in Bamako: three criminal cases presented by the National Police, several suspects arrested. National Police of Mali, Youssouf Koné, Broulaye Doumbia, Mouctar Fofana, Boubacar Ly, police investigation, Sébénikoro, ACI 2000, Djélibougou, security in Mali. National Police of Mali, Youssouf Koné, Broulaye Doumbia, Mouctar Fofana, Boubacar Ly, police investigation, Sébénikoro, ACI 2000, Djélibougou, security in Mali . Contact us ✍️ Writing [email protected] Advertising and partnerships [email protected] Facebook (Bamada.net) https://www.facebook.com/Bamada.net 2. Bamako: three murder cases solved by the police. Bamako, October 28 (AMAP) The National Police has clarified three cases of murders and assassinations that occurred recently in Bamako, with the arrest of several suspects within 24 to 48 hours. The Director General of the National Police, Comptroller General Youssouf Koné, presented the results of the investigations on Wednesday at a press briefing held at the Directorate General of the National Police (DGPN), noted AMAP . 3. Operation Dougoukoloko: two terrorist positions neutralized in the Timbuktu and Segou regions. Bamako, October 28 (AMAP) The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, neutralized two positions of regroupment of terrorist elements on October 26 and 27, 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, announced Wednesday the General Staff of the Armed Forces According to the statement, the surveillance and reconnaissance operations carried out on October 26 made it possible to locate, about 75 kilometers northwest of Léré, in the Timbuktu region, about fifteen terrorist elements grouped under a shelter.

Burkina Faso: 4 retained reports. 1. Burkina Faso. War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity in Burkina Faso by All Sides Burkina Faso In January 2022, army officers under the self-proclaimed Patriotic Movement for Safeguard and Restoration (Le mouvement patriotique pour la sauvegarde et la restauration, MPSR) staged a coup against President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré, who had been elected for a second term in 2020. 2. The MGDP hosts the 2nd session of the Joint Monitoring Committee for Military and Technical Cooperation Egypt-Burkina Faso. The Ministry of War and Patriotic Defence (MGDP) hosted, on 27 October 2026 in Ouagadougou, the opening ceremony of the second session of the Joint Monitoring Committee for Military and Technical Cooperation between the Arab Republic of Egypt and Burkina Faso. Scheduled over two days, the work was opened by the Comrade Secretary General of the MGDP, Intendant Colonel-Major Yamba Léonard OUOBA . 3. Burkina Faso Restores Death Penalty. Burkina Faso’s unelected parliament has unanimously adopted a new penal code that restores the death penalty for high treason, terrorism, acts of espionage, parricide and importation of expired or prohibited products. The country had abolished the death penalty for ordinary crimes in 2018 while its last known judicial execution took place in 1988. Reinstating capital punishment sends a chilling message to critics of the military junta and risks becoming another tool to suppress dissent.

Niger: 15 retained reports. 1. A strategic turning point. L’approbation par le Parlement algérien du déploiement de troupes au Niger marque un tournant majeur dans les relations entre les deux pays. Au-delà de son caractère historique pour Alger, cette décision traduit une volonté de renforcer la coopération sécuritaire dans un Sahel confronté à la persistance des violences terroristes, à la criminalité transfrontalière. 2. Tillabéri: riders of tricycles and motorcycles adeydeyta announce a 48-hour strike. In a notice dated 27 October 2026 and addressed to the managing director of the urban municipality, the Syndicat national des taxis tricycles du Niger (SNTTN), Tillabéri section, announces a work stoppage from Sunday 1 to Monday 2 November 2026. Through this walkout, they intend to protest against the measures restricting traffic in certain areas, taken by the authorities for safety reasons . 3. Chadian drone strike in the Agadez region: Chadian ambassador to Niger summoned to the office of the Minister of Foreign Affairs. Niamey, Oct 27 (ANP)- The Minister of Justice, Keeper of the Seals, Mr. Alio Daouda, acting Minister of Foreign Affairs, Cooperation and Nigeriens Abroad, received this Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Ambassador of the Republic of Chad in Niger, after the drone strike of his country occurred in the region of Agadez (Niger) This measure follows a drone airstrike that occurred on October 24, 2026, around 1 a.m., in the Emiloulou area, Agadez region.

Mali.title: Mali: A convoy of 1107 tankers filled with fuel arrives in Bamako
Mali.summary: Mali: A convoy of 1107 fuel-filled tankers arrives in Bamako In Mali, the state continues to ensure fuel supply in the capital Bamako and the rest of the country. On the morning of yesterday, Monday, October 26, 2026, an impressive convoy of 1,107 tanker trucks filled with fuel arrived in the city of the three caimans ,under military escort . This is the largest convoy that Bamako has hosted since the beginning of this month of October, according to the Directorate General of Trade, Consumer Affairs and Competition.

Mali.title: Macina: humanitarian emergency intensifies for 542 displaced people from Souleye
Mali.summary: Fleeing the attack on their village on September 3, 542 residents of Souleye, in the Ségou region, found refuge in Macina. Saturated houses, lack of food and difficulties in accessing school and social services: there are many needs. Despite the solidarity of local populations and the support of humanitarians, reception conditions remain difficult Forced to flee in a hurry, Souleye residents abandoned their homes, property and livelihoods.

Mali.title: Tafouk TV, the new media arm of Moscow-backed Sahelian juntas
Mali.summary: Launched by the military regimes of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, Tafouk TV aims to impose the Alliance of Sahel States’ sovereignty-focused narrative. Encouraged by Russia, the broadcaster is emerging as repression against local journalists intensifies.

Mali.title: Mali: Thirteen civilians killed by an army drone strike, in the Timbuktu region
Mali.summary: In Mali, thirteen civilians, including six children, were killed on the night of Sunday to Monday, October 26, by a drone strike by the Malian army, near Lerneb, in the Timbuktu region, according to information verified by RFI from many local sources. The General Staff did not communicate about this strike . The Malian army, together with its Russian partners in the Africa Corps, is fighting jihadist or pro-independence groups active in the country.

Mali.title: Ukraine Allegedly Supporting Mali Militia
Mali.summary: Ukraine is facing questions over its alleged involvement in supporting Tuareg fighters in northern Mali, a development that could extend its rivalry with Russia into Africa's Sahel region. A September 2026 CNN investigation reported that around 15 Ukrainian drone specialists were assisting Tuareg fighters, although DW said it had not independently verified the claims and Ukraine has not confirmed a specific operation.

Mali.title: Bamako: when violent death and disappearances become a worrying reality
Mali.summary: On the banks of the Djoliba, October ends in pain: a woman who was allegedly killed by her husband only a week after their marriage, a young shopkeeper found slaughtered in his shop in Commune I, young people invited to nocturnal meetings then found dead in the ACI sector or near the market Les Halles de Bamako In addition to these tragedies, disappearances have become too frequent in the city of the Three Caymans.

Mali.title: Mali: Why Ukraine May Be Involved in Mali's Conflict
Mali.summary: Allegations that Ukrainian specialists are supporting Tuareg rebels in Mali highlight Kyiv's effort to challenge Russian influence far beyond the battlefield in Europe. Ukraine is fighting Russia — and the conflict may extend into Africa's Sahel region. According to an investigation published by US media outlet CNN in September, around 15 Ukrainian drone specialists are reportedly supporting Tuareg rebels in northern Mali.

Mali.source: AMAP (Agence Malienne de Presse et de Publicité)
Mali.title: Cooperation: Accra and Bamako consolidate their strategic and economic partnership
Mali.summary: Bamako, October 27 (AMAP) Ghana's new ambassador to Mali, Lieutenant-Colonel Umar Sanda Ahmed, who was received in audience on Monday by the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, placed his mission under the sign of security cooperation, the opening up of Mali via Ghanaian ports and respect for the sovereignty and principles of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), noted AMAP The Ghanaian diplomat reaffirmed his country's commitment to regional security as well as its firm commitment alongside Mali in the fight against insecurity and violent extremism .

Mali.title: Menaka: CNDH condemns attacks on civilians in Tagadayat
Mali.summary: The National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) has condemned attacks on civilian populations in a camp in Tagadayat, in the Menaka region. In a statement, she said she is deeply concerned about these serious human rights violations, offers her condolences to the families of the victims and wishes a speedy recovery to the injured . The CNDH calls on the authorities to search for and bring to justice the perpetrators, sponsors and accomplices of these attacks.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: 12 Beninese arrested in an alleged fraud case
Burkina Faso.summary: Douze ressortissants béninois sont interpellés à Gaoua, dans le sud-ouest du Burkina Faso. Ils sont soupçonnés d’avoir monté deux réseaux d’arnaque qui profitaient de la crédulité de personnes en quête de protection selon l’Agence d’Information du Burkina Faso. Les interpellations ont eu lieu les 21 et 22 octobre 2026, a annoncé mardi le chef du Service régional de la police judiciaire (SRPJ) du Djôrô, le capitaine Théophile Zongo.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: 12 suspected crooks arrested in Gaoua
Burkina Faso.summary: Twelve suspected fraudsters of Beninese nationality were arrested on 21 and 22 October 2026 in Gaoua in south-west Burkina Faso by the Regional Judicial Police Service (SRPJ) of Djôrô, reports the AIB, on Tuesday 27 October.

Burkina Faso.title: Justice. In Burkina Faso, a new Penal Code reinstates the death penalty International mail
Burkina Faso.summary: Abolished in 2018, then mentioned again in December 2025, the death penalty was reinstated in the new version of the Burkinabe Criminal Code adopted by the deputies on October 20. It must now be promulgated by the President, Ibrahim Traoré. The death penalty “is provided in particular for acts of terrorism, treason, espionage, assassination, parricide and certain other serious crimes,” details Studio Yafa The text provides for the execution of this sentence, "shooting, lethal injection, hanging or electrocution", adds the media of the Swallow Foundation.

Burkina Faso.title: Cybercrime: “Paying a ransom funds the next attack and guarantees nothing”, Dr Karim Ganamé, Cybersecurity Specialist
Burkina Faso.summary: Cybercrime: “Paying a ransom funds the next attack and guarantees nothing”, Dr. Karim Ganamé, Cybersecurity Specialist Ransomware attacks are a growing threat to businesses, governments and critical infrastructure Behind these cyberattacks sometimes lurk real criminal organizations, structured like businesses, who take their victims' data hostage and demand ransoms of up to several million dollars.

Burkina Faso.title: Road safety: The agent's gesture takes precedence over the traffic light
Burkina Faso.summary: Road safety: The gesture of the agent takes precedence over the traffic light In road traffic, signs, traffic lights and ground markings play an essential role in the organization of travel. But when an agent authorized to regulate traffic intervenes, his instructions may prevail over the indications of the automatic devices . A rule sometimes unknown to some users, as illustrated by a scene observed in Ouagadougou, not far from the palace of Larlé Naaba.

Niger.title: Niger denounces a drone attack by Chad with "the support of France"
Niger.summary: The facts date back to October 24 at 1am in the Emi Lulu area, in the Agadez region, not far from the Algerian border. This drone strike was carried out "from Chad" with "the support of France", according to the Nigerien government and left two civilians dead and wounded . Niamey speaks of an act of aggression, a violation of his national sovereignty and announces referral to the United Nations Security Council, the Peace and Security Council of the African Union invoking the UN Charter and the founding principles of the AU.

Niger.title: Chadian drone strikes in Niger: CODDAE calls for increased vigilance at national level
Niger.summary: Niamey, Oct 27 (ANP)- The Collective for the Defense of the Right to Energy CODDAE issued a press release on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, denouncing the aggression of the drone from Chad during the night of October 24 to 25 that hit the Emi Lulu area. This attack, the statement reports, “clearly seeks to open a new front against Niger and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), which strengthens our sacred union” To this end, the Collective calls on the Nigerien population to strengthen national vigilance in the face of this attempt to sow terror.

Niger.title: Image Africa Niger: Chad denies any involvement in "drone strikes" on its soil with the "support" of France
Niger.summary: On Tuesday, October 27, Chad rejected accusations from Niger, a neighboring country with which relations have been tense for several months. The latter accuses him of having killed two civilians in a "drone strike" on Nigerien soil with the "support" of France. Through its spokesperson, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, N’Djamena categorically denied Niamey's accusations about a drone strike on Nigerian soil on Monday, October 26 .

Niger.title: Why relations are deteriorating between Niger and Chad
Niger.summary: The Nigerien government once again accuses Chad and France of having carried out hostile action on its territory. According to Niamey, a drone strike in the Agadez region, near the Algerian border, killed two civilians and injured several others. The Nigerien authorities claim that the operation was carried out from Chadian territory with the support of France .

Niger.title: A new rift in the coast.. A crisis between Niamey and N'Djamena in which the threads of Paris are intertwined
Niger.summary: In a new escalation that has restored tension and congestion to the Sahel region of Africa, Niger on Monday evening filed a complaint before the United Nations against Chad, summoning N'Djamena's ambassador to it, after accusing its neighbor of launching a drone strike on its territory, which left deaths and injuries as well as material damage. . The escalation not only accused N'Djamena of violating sovereignty and supporting those she described as “mercenaries,” but also took on a deeper regional character, with Niger pointing the finger directly at Paris and its attempts to reposition its lost influence.

Niger.title: Niger Strike: Chad Denies Involvement and Demands Evidence
Niger.summary: Relations between Chad and Niger escalated on 26 October. Niamey accused his neighbor of carrying out a drone strike in the Agadez region with the complicity of France. The reaction of the Chadian government was not long in coming Indeed, on Tuesday, October 27, N 'djamena denied any involvement in this operation and asked the Nigerien authorities to present the elements on which their accusations are based.

Niger.title: Drone strike on Agadez: Chad reacts to Niger's accusations
Niger.summary: Chad does not admit to conducting a drone strike on Emi loulou (hill in the Agadez region) on Saturday, October 24. He firmly rejected these accusations of Niamey, in a statement read this Tuesday, October 27 by his Minister of Communication, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, on national television . The Nigerien authorities invited to make public the evidence they say N’Djaména is holding assures that he has "in no way ordered, conducted or supported any air military operation from his soil against Niger" .

Niger.title: The Interregional Service of the Judicial Police dismantles three criminal gangs
Niger.summary: Zinder, Oct 26 (ANP)- The Zinder Judicial Police has dismantled three networks of young criminals specializing in night robberies, in the city and its surroundings. The thugs were presented Tuesday, October 26 to the media with a large amount of stolen objects . The three specialized gangs that operate in the riverside neighborhoods benefit from the complicity of a concealer woman who was arrested just as she was about to leave Zinder for a neighboring country.

Niger.title: Chad-Niger: a new escalation between Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno and Abdourahamane Tiani
Niger.summary: Niamey accuses N’Djamena of having launched a drone strike on its territory, with the support of France. A charge that rekindles distrust between the two neighbors. Published today at 16:57, modified at 20:39 Reading: 5 minutes.

Niger.title: Niger: Niamey accuses Chad and France after a drone strike
Niger.summary: The Nigerien territory was targeted, on October 24, 2026 at around 1 a.m., by a drone strike carried out from Chadian territory with the "support" of France, informs a statement from the government of Niamey read on public television. According to the announcement, made on October 26, 2026, the attack left two civilians dead, several wounded . The drone strike also damaged vehicles in the Agadez region, near the Algerian border.

Niger.title: Agadez: The governor chairs the regular meeting of the CRS and visits the wounded from the attack on two SONITRAV buses
Niger.summary: The Governor of the Agadez region, Major General Ibra Boulama Issa, chaired, on October 21, 2026, the regular meeting of the Regional Security Council (CRS) devoted to the review of the security situation in the region and the events following the attack perpetrated on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 by armed bandits against two SONITRAV buses, on the Tchirozérine-Agadez axis At the end of this meeting, the governor, accompanied by the members of the CRS, went to the Regional Hospital Center (CHR) of Agadez to inquire about the state of health of the wounded and to show the compassion of the country's authorities to…

Niger.title: Working visit of the Minister of State, Minister of National Defence to Algeria: Niamey and Algiers strengthen their security cooperation for the protection of their common interests
Niger.summary: Depuis, la visite du Général d’Armée Abdourahamane Tiani à Alger en février 2026, l’Algérie et le Niger renforcent leur coopération, notamment dans le domaine de la Défense et de la Sécurité, lui donnant ainsi une dimension stratégique. C’est dans le cadre de cette nouvelle dynamique que le Ministre d’État, Ministre de la Défense Nationale, le Général d’Armée Salifou Mody a effectué une visite de travail à Alger, le mardi 20 octobre 2026, accompagné d’une délégation d’experts du Ministère de la Défense Nationale.

Niger.title: Official statement of the government following a drone strike in Nigerian territory by Chad
Niger.summary: The Government informs national and international opinion that on October 24, 2026, at around 1 a.m., the national territory was the target of a drone airstrike carried out from the territory of Chad in the Emiloulou area, Agadez region, with the support of a foreign power, France. This strike resulted in the death of two civilians and injuries. It also damaged vehicles .

Niger.title: Hostile act: N’Djamena rejects Niamey's accusations and demands evidence
Niger.summary: The Chadian government firmly rejected, on Tuesday, October 27, Niger's accusations attributing to it a deadly drone strike that occurred on October 24 in the Agadez region, which the Nigerien authorities described, the day before, as a "hostile act" In a statement read on national television, government spokesman Gassim Chérif Mahamat demanded evidence from Niamey and announced that N’Djamena was in favour of an independent international investigation.

Niger.title: Accusations of strikes in Niger: Chad denies and demands proof of Niamey
Niger.summary: The tone rises between N’Djamena and Niamey. The Chadian government on Tuesday rejected accusations by the Nigerien authorities that a drone strike carried out from Chadian territory targeted an area of the Agadez region on the night of 24 October, causing the death of two civilians and injuring several others, according to the toll announced by Niamey In a statement read on national television, the Minister of Communication and government spokesman, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, assured that Chad had "in no way ordered, conducted or supported" an air military operation against Niger.

Niger.title: Territorial aggression in Niger: Niamey accuses Chad and France after a drone strike and seizes the UN
Niger.summary: In an official statement issued on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Government of the Republic of Niger denounced an airstrike that targeted its national territory on the night of October 24. Balance sheet, two civilians killed and several wounded. Directly accusing Chad and France, the Nigerien authorities announced a battery of diplomatic, judicial and security responses .

Niger.title: Niger: Niamey blames Chad and France after deadly drone strike
Niger.summary: Niger: Niamey accuses Chad and France after a deadly drone strike The Nigerien government claims that its territory was targeted, Saturday around 00:00 GMT, by an airstrike carried out by drone from Chad, with the alleged support of France. The attack reportedly took place in the Emi Lulu area, in the Agadez region, near the Algerian border According to the Niamey authorities, the strike left two civilians dead, several injured and damaged vehicles.

Niger.summary: Algerian soldiers are due to reach the Madama base in northern Niger, "Jeune Afrique" reported on Sunday. This place near Libya had been set up by the French army from 2014 to monitor the roads of armed groups, before being put to sleep in 2023. Madama military base in Niger Madama is about to wake up from its sleep with a new military partner According to information reported by our colleagues from Jeune Afrique, Algerian units are to be deployed in this base located a hundred kilometers from the Libyan border, at the request of the Nigerien authorities.

Niger.title: Niger: The country denounces a drone attack by Chad with "the support of France"
Niger.summary: Niger summons Chad's ambassador following a drone strike on its territory. In a statement read on national television on Monday, October 26, the Nigerien government denounced "a drone airstrike carried out from the territory of Chad" and in which, according to it, France participated. Niger.title: Niger: Niamey accuses Chad of a drone strike that killed two people

Niger.title: Niger: two civilians killed in drone strike, Niamey accuses Chad and France

Niger.title: Niger accuses Chad of deadly drone attack in which two civilians died

Mali: A convoy of 1107 fuel-filled tankers arrives in Bamako In Mali, the state continues to ensure fuel supply in the capital Bamako and the rest of the country. On the morning of yesterday, Monday, October 26, 2026, an impressive convoy of 1,107 tanker trucks filled with fuel arrived in the city of the three caimans ,under military escort . This is the largest convoy that Bamako has hosted since the beginning of this month of October, according to the Directorate General of Trade, Consumer Affairs and Competition. 2. Macina: humanitarian emergency intensifies for 542 displaced people from Souleye. Fleeing the attack on their village on September 3, 542 residents of Souleye, in the Ségou region, found refuge in Macina. Saturated houses, lack of food and difficulties in accessing school and social services: there are many needs. Despite the solidarity of local populations and the support of humanitarians, reception conditions remain difficult Forced to flee in a hurry, Souleye residents abandoned their homes, property and livelihoods. 3. Tafouk TV, the new media arm of Moscow-backed Sahelian juntas. Launched by the military regimes of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, Tafouk TV aims to impose the Alliance of Sahel States’ sovereignty-focused narrative. Encouraged by Russia, the broadcaster is emerging as repression against local journalists intensifies.

Burkina Faso: 5 retained reports. 1. Burkina Faso: 12 Beninese arrested in an alleged fraud case. Douze ressortissants béninois sont interpellés à Gaoua, dans le sud-ouest du Burkina Faso. Ils sont soupçonnés d’avoir monté deux réseaux d’arnaque qui profitaient de la crédulité de personnes en quête de protection selon l’Agence d’Information du Burkina Faso. Les interpellations ont eu lieu les 21 et 22 octobre 2026, a annoncé mardi le chef du Service régional de la police judiciaire (SRPJ) du Djôrô, le capitaine Théophile Zongo. 2. Burkina Faso: 12 suspected crooks arrested in Gaoua. Twelve suspected fraudsters of Beninese nationality were arrested on 21 and 22 October 2026 in Gaoua in south-west Burkina Faso by the Regional Judicial Police Service (SRPJ) of Djôrô, reports the AIB, on Tuesday 27 October. 3. Justice. In Burkina Faso, a new Penal Code reinstates the death penalty International mail. Abolished in 2018, then mentioned again in December 2025, the death penalty was reinstated in the new version of the Burkinabe Criminal Code adopted by the deputies on October 20. It must now be promulgated by the President, Ibrahim Traoré. The death penalty “is provided in particular for acts of terrorism, treason, espionage, assassination, parricide and certain other serious crimes,” details Studio Yafa The text provides for the execution of this sentence, "shooting, lethal injection, hanging or electrocution", adds the media of the Swallow Foundation.

The facts date back to October 24 at 1am in the Emi Lulu area, in the Agadez region, not far from the Algerian border. This drone strike was carried out "from Chad" with "the support of France", according to the Nigerien government and left two civilians dead and wounded . Niamey speaks of an act of aggression, a violation of his national sovereignty and announces referral to the United Nations Security Council, the Peace and Security Council of the African Union invoking the UN Charter and the founding principles of the AU. 2. Niamey, Oct 27 (ANP)- The Collective for the Defense of the Right to Energy CODDAE issued a press release on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, denouncing the aggression of the drone from Chad during the night of October 24 to 25 that hit the Emi Lulu area. This attack, the statement reports, “clearly seeks to open a new front against Niger and the Alliance of Sahel States (AES), which strengthens our sacred union” To this end, the Collective calls on the Nigerien population to strengthen national vigilance in the face of this attempt to sow terror. 3. Image Africa Niger: Chad denies any involvement in "drone strikes" on its soil with the "support" of France. On Tuesday, October 27, Chad rejected accusations from Niger, a neighboring country with which relations have been tense for several months. The latter accuses him of having killed two civilians in a "drone strike" on Nigerien soil with the "support" of France. Through its spokesperson, Gassim Chérif Mahamat, N’Djamena categorically denied Niamey's accusations about a drone strike on Nigerian soil on Monday, October 26 .

Niger.title: Algeria To Deploy Troops To Niger In First Foreign Mission In 53 Years

Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria.

Niger.title: Tillabéri/Infrastructure: Minister Salissou Mahaman Salissou assesses the work of the Farié-Téra road and the impact of the Garbougna structure
Niger.summary: The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, made a visit on Friday, October 23, 2026, to the Farié-Téra axis, in the Tillabéri region. On the agenda, the monitoring of the rehabilitation work of this road and the evaluation of a crossing structure built in Garbougna to end the seasonal isolation of this locality . Through these two stages, the Minister took stock of the achievements, the remaining work and the measures taken to continue the work in a difficult security context.

Niger.title: Algerian parliament approves army deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: A military parade takes place during the 2026 graduation ceremony at the Houari-Boumediene Military Academy in Cherchell, Algeria on July 9, 2026. /VCG File Algerian lawmakers on Sunday approved deploying People's National Army detachments to Niger, according to official statements from both chambers of parliament. During closed-door sessions, Algeria's Council of the Nation and People's National Assembly, the upper and lower houses of parliament, respectively, validated the presidential notification submitted by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune under Article 91 of the Constitution.

Niger.title: Algerian upper house of parliament approves troop deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: Algeria’s upper house of parliament has approved deploying troops to Niger to protect its energy facilities. The country’s Council of Nations approved the deployment during an emergency session on Sunday, while the lower house is expected to hold a session on Monday. If the deployment is approved in the lower parliament, it means the country is highly likely to deploy troops to protect its facilities located along the border area in the north of Niger, particularly the Kafra oil region and other energy facilities linked to Algeria’s state-owned energy company Sonatrach.

Niger.title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment in over 50 years
Niger.summary: Algeria’s parliament on Sunday approved a resolution to send troops to Niger, making the first time Algerian soldiers will be deployed abroad since the 1973 Arab-Israeli war. Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups, including near its border with Algeria, and the deployment comes as Algiers and Niamey are building the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline after decades of delays.

Niger.title: Algeria’s military deployment to Niger: What’s behind the move?
Niger.summary: Algeria’s parliament has approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger, in a major shift in the North African nation’s noninterventionist military doctrine. Algeria’s lower house, the People’s National Assembly, ratified the deployment on Sunday after the upper house, the Council of the Nation, unanimously approved the proposal earlier in the day.

Niger.title: Africa: Algerian soldiers in Niger
Niger.summary: The Algerian Parliament unanimously approved on Sunday the deployment of units of the National People's Army in Niger. This would be Algeria's first military intervention abroad since sending troops in support of Egypt during the 1973 war . Algerian soldiers are to settle in Madama, in northern Niger, near the Libyan border, on the site of a former French base used during Operation Barkhane.

Niger.title: Algeria: Parliament approves deployment of troops to Niger
Niger.summary: On Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Algerian Parliament approved the sending of army units to Niger. This decision, which marks a break with the traditional doctrine of military non-intervention abroad, aims in particular to protect Algerian energy interests in the Sahelian country, Al Jazeera reports. Algeria reaches a major milestone in its military cooperation with Niger .

Niger.title: Sahel: Algerian parliament authorizes sending troops to Niger
Niger.summary: Algeria is taking a new step in its security rapprochement with Niger. On Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Council of the Nation, the upper chamber of the Algerian Parliament, unanimously approved a decision authorizing the dispatch of a detachment of the National People's Army (ANP) to Niger This initiative comes in a context of strengthening military cooperation between Algiers and Niamey, against the backdrop of security threats in the Sahel and strategic economic interests.

Niger.title: Military Adventure in Niger Threatens Algeria with Drowning in 'Swamp Coast'
Niger.summary: Algeria is venturing into one of the most volatile security environments in Africa, after the parliamentary approval announced on Sunday opened the door to sending army units to Niger, in a move that is difficult to separate from the decline of its diplomatic influence in the Sahel region, and its attempt to restore a regional position that has become vulnerable to changing alliances and escalating competition among external powers.

Niger.title: Algerian parliament votes to send soldiers to neighboring Niger
Niger.summary: The Council of the Nation, the upper house, and then the National People's Assembly, the lower house, both voted on Sunday to send military troops to Niger.

Niger.title: Border security and energy interests.. What is behind Algeria's decision to send troops to Niger?
Niger.summary: The Algerian parliament, in its two chambers, the People's National Assembly and the National Assembly, on Sunday, approved the request of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune to send units of the Algerian army to Niger, with the aim of protecting the strategic interests of the country and securing the investment projects of the state company Sonatrach, in response to a request from the Nigerian authorities.

Niger.title: Nigerien, 3 others nabbed over guard’s killing, theft
Niger.summary: Operatives of the Edo State Police Command have arrested a Niger Republic national and three others over the alleged killing of a security guard and theft of goods worth over N400 million in the state. The suspects, identified as Hamisu Nuhu, Suleiman Rabiu, Hussaini Gago, a Nigerien, and Ibrahim Haruna, were arrested in connection with a robbery at Paparazzi Communication Complex in Auchi, Etsako West Local Government Area, on July 12, 2026.

Mali.title: Mali: the death toll from last weekend's deadly attack rises to 54 (army)
Mali.summary: The Malian armed forces announced on Saturday that they had discovered 54 bodies after attacks on camps in the north-east of the country last weekend, bringing the death toll to six more. The attacks targeted the Menaka region of the troubled West African country, where gunmen reportedly arrived on motorcycles before opening fire on camps mainly housing members of the Daoussahak community It was within the Daoussahak community that the Armed Movement for the Salvation of Azawad (MSA), a group allied to the ruling junta in Mali, was born, according to security and community sources.

Mali.title: Mali: the Directorate of Human Resources of the Armed Forces towards a new status
Mali.summary: The Council of Ministers adopted a draft law amending the ordinance of 27 September 2017 establishing the Directorate of Human Resources of the Armed Forces (DRHA). The decision aims to adapt this structure to the reforms undertaken to modernize the Malian Armed Forces . Created to develop and monitor the implementation of the human resources management and development policy, the HRD faces shortcomings related to the evolution of the institutional and legal framework as well as the new requirements of the army.

Mali.title: Mali military reports 54 dead after attacks in northeast
Mali.summary: Mali's armed forces say the death toll from attacks on camps in the country's northeastern Menaka region has risen to 54, after six more bodies were discovered. The attacks occurred last weekend when armed men on motorcycles reportedly opened fire on camps mainly occupied by members of the Daoussahak community. A general view of a damaged school near the Kidal regional headquarters in Kidal, Mali, May 9, 2026.

Mali.title: Menaka: 54 bodies found after terrorist attacks in Tagayat
Mali.summary: Bamako, 25 October (AMAP) The State – Major General of the Armed Forces informs the Opinion that on the basis of reports of a terrorist attack on civilian populations in the operational sub-sector of Menaka, a joint FAMa- Partners patrol has been launched on the ground During this search, the patrol discovered, about 35 km southeast of the city of Menaka fifty-four (54) lifeless bodies in a camp in Tagayat.

Mali.title: KIDAL: the FAMa provide care and comfort to the populations of the camps
Mali.summary: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), through the Directorate of the Armed Forces Health Service (DSSA) and their Russian partner, conducted, on Friday, October 23, 2026, a medical assistance operation for the benefit of the populations living in the localities located on the outskirts of the city of Kidal .

Mali.title: Mali: HRW accuses army of beating civilians, JNIM refuses to punish execution of prisoners
Mali.summary: Human Rights Watch (HRW) published an investigation into abuses since July in central and northern Mali on Monday, October 19. The NGO documents indiscriminate drone strikes by the Malian army and the execution of soldiers captured by JNIM and the Fla. HRW turns to the African Union, for lack of other interlocutor .

Niger.title: Sending a detachment of the Algerian army to Niger.. New details
Niger.summary: The PNA received parliamentary and political authorization to send a detachment to Niger to protect and secure crews and energy projects for the Sonatrach International Exploration and Production Branch (Cepax).

Niger.title: Military cooperation: at the request of Niamey, Algeria will deploy soldiers in Niger
Niger.summary: Convened in emergency session by decree of Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune, the Council of the Nation (Senate) and the National People's Assembly, the lower chamber, both chambers of Parliament, unanimously approved the request for authorization of the deployment of Algerian military troops in Niger With this agreement of the Parliament, at the request of the Nigerien authorities according to Algiers, Algeria activates for the first time paragraph 2 of Article 91 of its 2020 Constitution and takes a major strategic step in its regional security doctrine .

Niger.title: Algeria: Senate approves sending troops to Niger
Niger.summary: The Council of the Nation, the upper chamber of the Algerian Parliament, voted unanimously on Sunday 25 October to send a detachment of the People's National Army (ANP) to Niger, reports the Algerian daily El Khabar. The decision was adopted at a special session devoted to a request by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune According to the Algerian media TSA, the planned deployment aims to ensure the protection of the oil investments of the public company Sonatrach in northern Niger.

Niger.title: Algeria moves to send troops to Niger to protect energy assets in historic policy shift The upper house of parliament backs a proposed overseas deployment as Algiers deepens security ties with Niamey and seeks to safeguard strategic projects, including a planned gas pipeline linking Nigeria to European markets.
Niger.summary: Algeria’s upper house of parliament on Sunday approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger to protect energy facilities, marking a potential turning point in the country’s long-standing policy of military non-intervention beyond its borders. A senator, speaking to AFP on condition of anonymity, said 148 members of the 174-seat Council of the Nation voted in favour of the measure.

Niger.title: Algeria: Parliament unanimously votes on a decision to send army units to Niger The decision to send Algerian troops to Niger came four days after the signing of a memorandum of understanding to strengthen military cooperation between Algiers and Niamey.
Niger.summary: The Council of the Nation, the upper chamber of the Algerian parliament, unanimously adopted a decision on Sunday to send military units to Niger. Convened for an extraordinary closed session, the Algerian senators thus agree to a profound change in Algerian military doctrine that prohibited the intervention of the army outside the country's borders . The same decision will be submitted, in the afternoon, to the National People's Congress (NPC), the lower house of parliament, for a similar vote.

Niger.title: Algeria Senate Approves Troop Deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: Algeria’s upper house of parliament has approved a proposal to deploy troops to neighbouring Niger to protect energy facilities, a senator said on Sunday. The senator, who spoke to AFP on condition of anonymity, said 148 of the 174 members of the upper house voted in favour of the proposal. Algeria’s lower house is expected to vote on the measure later on Sunday.

Niger.title: A detachment of the Algerian army in Niger.. What is the nature of the mission?
Niger.summary: Today, the National Assembly unanimously approved the request of the President of the Republic to send a detachment of the Algerian army to the State of Niger. The vote came after the President of the Republic was notified of the request to approve the dispatch of the army detachment in order to protect the investment projects of "Sonatrach" International "Cepax" at the request of the State of Niger.

Niger.title: Algeria will deploy soldiers to Niger after a unanimous vote in the Senate
Niger.summary: A unit of the People's National Army (ANP) will soon leave for Niger. Indeed, this Sunday, October 25, 2026, the upper house of the Parliament of Algeria, voted unanimously in favor of this dispatch, decided by President Abdelmadjid Tebboune. For the time being, the authorities have not communicated either the number of soldiers or the duration of the deployment But according to parliamentarians quoted by the Algerian press and taken over by the Anadolu agency, the detachment would be responsible for protecting Sonatrach oil projects in Niger.

Niger.title: Algerian parliament’s upper house approves troop deployment to Niger
Niger.summary: The upper house of Algeria’s parliament has unanimously approved the deployment of troops to neighbouring Niger. The Algerian constitution empowers the president to send military units abroad, provided that both chambers of parliament approve it by a two-thirds majority. Niger.summary: The Algerian National Assembly, the upper house of parliament, voted unanimously on Sunday to send units of the People's National Army to Niger, in a move that is considered a first in the Algerian army's extraterritorial tasks since the October 1973 war.

Niger.title: Two European women kidnapped in Niger freed in Libya
Niger.summary: An Austrian and a Swiss women kidnapped in Niger more than a year and a half ago have been freed and are in Libya, Bern and Vienna announced Thursday. Sixty-nine-year-old Swiss national Claudia Abbt and 76-year-old Eva Gretzmacher arrived in the eastern city of Benghazi where they received medical treatment. Their release follows an intervention by Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, who controls the east and parts of the south of the country.

Mali.title: Mali Army, Russian Fighters Accused of Civilian Killings
Mali.summary: Human Rights Watch has accused Mali's armed forces and Russia-controlled Africa Corps of committing serious abuses against civilians in the central Mopti region during renewed fighting. The organisation said an apparent military drone strike on September 16 killed eight civilians and injured at least six others in Guélédié village. Witnesses reported that the strike hit an area where residents had gathered to access satellite internet, although armed fighters linked to al-Qaeda were reportedly present in the village.

Mali.title: Mali – Qatar: General Daoud Aly Mohammedine and the Qatari diplomat discuss security cooperation
Mali.summary: MALI QATAR: TOWARDS STRENGTHENING SECURITY COOPERATION The Minister of Security and Civil Protection, Major General Daoud Aly MOHAMMEDINE, received in audience, this Thursday, October 22, 2026, His Excellency Ahmed Turki A. A. ALSOBAI, new Ambassador of the State of Qatar in Mali .

Mali.title: Mali: Army, Russia's 'Africa Corps' Commit New Abuses
Mali.summary: Nairobi — Unlawful Drone Strike, Torture of Civilians in Mopti Region Mali's armed forces and the allied Russia-controlled Africa Corps have committed new atrocities against civilians in central Mali during renewed fighting, Human Rights Watch said today. On September 16, 2026, an apparent military drone strike in Guélédié village, Mopti region, killed eight civilians and injured at least six others.

Mali.title: Mali: More than forty civilians killed on Sunday by armed men
Mali.summary: Mali : plus d'une quarantaine de civils tués dimanche par des hommes armés More than 40 civilians were killed on Sunday in attacks carried out by armed men in the Ménaka region of northeastern Mali, causing population displacements, several security, local and civil society sources told AFP on Monday. These bloody attacks, carried out by armed men arriving on motorcycles, targeted, according to these sources, several camps belonging mainly to the Daoussahak community, from which the armed movement "Movement for the Salvation of Azawad" (MSA), close to the junta in power in Bamako, originates.

Mali.title: Mali: more than forty civilians killed Sunday by armed men, according to security and local sources

Burkina Faso.title: Quarterly increase in the colours of the SDS: Burkinabe Customs at the rendezvous of patriotic duty

This solemn meeting, marked by patriotism and brotherhood of arms, was held in a context marked by the commemoration of the 66th anniversary of the National Armed Forces .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina/Solidarity: A member of the diaspora provides support to widows and orphans who are victims of the war

Burkina Faso.title: ‎Tenkodogo: Water and forest agents capture a crocodile near a chicken coop and release it into the dam
Burkina Faso.summary: Tenkodogo: Water and forestry officers capture a crocodile near a chicken coop and release it into the dam A crocodile lurking near a chicken coop in a courtyard in the Gommisi neighborhood, opposite the Tenkodogo Gendarmerie Group, was captured without incident on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and then released into the city dam . According to the Burkina news agency that reports the information, it was a resident who gave the alert to the competent services after seeing the reptile in the concession.

Niger.title: illabéri: the Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure visits the rehabilitation site of the Farié-Téra axis
Niger.summary: Tillabéri, Oct 23 (ANP) – The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou carried out, this Friday, October 23, 2026, a field visit to the rehabilitation site of the Farié-Téra road as well as at the Garbougna structure. Niger.title: Defense: In the field of military operations, the SDF continues to maintain pressure on armed terrorist groups
Niger.summary: Despite the relative lull observed recently in the fight against security threats, the defense and security forces (FDS) remain mobilized on the various fronts of military operations where they continue to maintain pressure against armed terrorist groups (AGT) and other organized criminal groups .

Niger.title: Algeria and Niger sign 'Memorandum of Understanding' to strengthen military cooperation
Niger.summary: Since the reconciliation at the beginning of the year between the President of Niger, Abdourahamane Tiani, and that of Algeria, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, Niamey and Algiers have not left each other: in the space of a month, this is the second time that leaders of the armies of the two countries have met. Niger.title: Tillabéri: the Minister of Equipment notes the progress of the work on the Farié-Téra road
Niger.summary: The Minister of Equipment and Infrastructure, Colonel-Major Salissou Mahaman Salissou, carried out this Friday, October 23, a field visit on the Fari-Tera road, in the Tillabéri region, to assess the progress of the rehabilitation work on this road and to note the state of a crossing work carried out in Garbou Gna for the benefit of the populations Accompanied by the Governor of the Tillabéri region, Colonel Maina Boukar, the Secretary General of the Governorate, officials of the Defence and Security Forces (FDS), the Prefect of the Department of Gothèye, as well as ministerial officials and departmental and…

Niger.title: Africa: Algeria and Niger sign "a memorandum of understanding" to strengthen their military cooperation
Niger.summary: The rapprochement between Algeria and Niger continues. After the visit of the President and the Prime Minister of Niger, the Minister of Defence was welcomed on 21 October in Algiers. With his Algerian counterpart, they signed a military agreement to strengthen security cooperation between the two countries This meeting comes barely two months after a mutiny in Niamey against the power of President Abdourahamane Tiani who has since received military support from Algiers.

Niger.title: Algeria-Niger: a military agreement that confirms the return of Algiers to the Sahel
Niger.summary: Algeria and Niger signed a memorandum of understanding on military cooperation on the occasion of the visit to Algiers of the Nigerien Minister of Defence, General Salifou Mody. Mali.title: Border coup: Algerian army shuts down Tinzaouaten and Timiaouine to track down traffickers
Mali.summary: Border coup: Algerian army closes Tinzaouaten and Timiaouine to hunt down traffickers The Algerian army has unleashed a vast security "grooming" operation on its border with Mali, targeting the smuggling of weapons and vehicles, as well as clandestine gold panning As part of this intensive deployment, the Tinzaouaten and Timiaouine border crossings were temporarily closed in order to facilitate controls and clean up the area.

Mali.title: AES – ECOWAS: What future for cooperation?
Mali.summary: The dialogue initiated in Dakar on 17 October should provide a sustainable framework for relations between the ESA and ECOWAS. The movement of people, trade and security call for concrete commitments between the two sets. Institutional separation has not erased interdependencies Since the effective withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from ECOWAS on 29 January 2025, the countries of both sets continue to share trade corridors, population movements and security challenges.

Mali.title: Arm of iron in Bamako: Seydou "Solution" against Mohamed "Lil Bougou", a contract signed on October 16

The two practitioners received a preparation bonus of 500,000 CFA francs each. The meeting, the date of which remains to be communicated, also provides for a bonus for the winner, the amount of which has not been made public .

Mali.title: Kayes: two suspects arrested for alleged supply of terrorist armed groups
Mali.summary: Kayes: two suspects arrested for an alleged supply of terrorist armed groups On 16 and 18 October 2026, the Police Station of the 2nd district of Kayes arrested two individuals suspected of supplying fuel to terrorist armed groups (GAT). Mali.summary: Mali: The FAMa hit a group of motorcyclists in the forest of Ouagadou The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) announce that they carried out a targeted strike on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, against a group of more than a dozen motorcyclists spotted in the forest of Ouagadou, near the village of Ngoma Koura According to our colleagues in Maliweb who cite the General Staff of the Armed Forces, several terrorist elements were neutralized during this operation carried out as part of Operation Dougoukoloko.
