Mali.summary: The General Staff of the Armed Forces informs the national opinion that the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing the permanent operations of surveillance, control and security of the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko . Mali.title: Securing the country: positions of armed groups hit in Niono and Dioura
Mali.summary: Bamako, 29 September (AMAP) The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, are continuing their operations to monitor, control and secure the national territory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, according to a statement from the General Staff of the Armed Forces issued on Tuesday The press release indicates that on Sunday, September 27, 2026, the exploitation of intelligence made it possible to locate, 13 km east of the city of Niono, a point of entrenchment of armed terrorist groups, among which were, according to the same source, perpetrators of an attack against an FAMa convoy.

Mali.title: Mali: "No one is spared", warns the NGO Amnesty in a report on the abuses of the army and the Wagner group
Mali.summary: "No one is spared": this is the title of the report published on 29 September by Amnesty International. The human rights organisation investigated cases of killings, torture and enforced disappearances committed by the Malian army and its Russian proxies. In particular, it documents the murders of at least 34 civilians in seven locations in Mali along the Mauritanian border between June 2023 and December 2025.

Mali.title: Sectors of Niono and Dioura: The FAMa strike several terrorist positions with precision

On Sunday, September 27, 2026, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 13 km east of the city of Niono, a point of entrenchment of armed terrorist groups among which were perpetrators of the attack on an FAMa convoy .

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: FAMa surgical strikes, several terrorist hideouts wiped out in the center of the country
Mali.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: Surgical strikes by the FAMa, several terrorist hideouts wiped out in the centre of the country By a statement issued on Tuesday, 29 September, the General Staff of the Armed Forces confirmed the continuation of the "Dougoukoloko" operation aimed at securing the territory. The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, conducted two rounds of targeted strikes on 27 and 28 September 2026 On Sunday, September 27, the exploitation of precise intelligence made it possible to locate, 13 km east of the city of Niono, a point of entrenchment of armed terrorist groups.

Mali.title: It targeted Arabs, Tuareg and Fulani.. Amnesty accuses Bamako and a Russian legion of war crimes
Mali.summary: Amnesty International has accused the Malian armed forces and elements of Russia's Africa Corps of committing war crimes during joint operations between June 2023 and December 2025. According to the organization, the crimes included killing, torturing and forcibly disappearing civilians and looting and destroying their property.

Mali.title: Mali: Russian army and paramilitaries accused of 'war crimes' by Amnesty International
Mali.summary: Members of the Malian Armed Forces (Fama) and the Russian paramilitary group Wagner committed “war crimes”, including “killings and torture”, against civilians in joint operations between 2023 and 2025, Amnesty International said in a new report published today. . The junta that has ruled Mali since two coups d 'état in 2020 and 2021 has turned to Russia to support it in its anti-jihadist struggle, in particular by calling on the services of the paramilitaries of the Wagner group, which in 2025 became the Africa Corps, under the control of the Russian Ministry of Defence .

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso: Junta-Led Government Inaugurates First Gold Refinery
Burkina Faso.summary: By Enyichukwu Enemanna The military-governed Burkina Faso has inaugurated its first gold refinery, as the West African country seeks to process more of its mineral resources locally and generate more revenue from its gold industry. According to a statement from the Communications Directorate of the Presidency of Faso, head of the junta government, President Ibrahim Traoré inaugurated the National Gold Refinery of Burkina Faso, known as RAFFINOR-BF, on Monday.

Burkina Faso.title: Burkina Faso opens first-ever gold refinery
Burkina Faso.summary: Burkina Faso opened its first gold refinery on Monday, pushing ahead with plans to better organise the commercialisation of the precious metal in one of the continent’s top producers. The West African nation is the continent’s third leading gold producer, churning out more than 94 tonnes of the precious metal last year, according to the World Gold Council. But authorities traditionally struggle to control the informal gold mining sector, which has been blighted by jihadist violence and smuggling.
